history.summary: THIS IS A SANAMAHI SHRINE (TRADITIONAL MEITEI RELIGION), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Pakhangba Temple (Pakhangba Laishang) stands on the hilltop of Uyal Cheirao Ching (also called Uyal Mamang Ching), a hill inside the Gwarok Reserved Forest in Thoubal district, Manipur; the CSV town 'Thoubal' is the district headquarters, corrected here to the nearest village, Uyal. It is dedicated to Ibudhou Pakhangba, a primordial deity of the Meitei pantheon, and also houses the shrine of Ibendhou Leisana. It is an important place of worship for followers of Sanamahism: rituals and ceremonies are performed annually by the Lai Committee, and devotees from nearby villages (Uyal, Wangbal, Kairembikhok, Wangjing, Salungpham, Heirok, Langmeithet, Icham Khunou) climb the hill to offer prayers; sacred clothes, ritual items and boulders inside the shrine hold special significance. The shrine has been vandalized more than once: in 2015 unknown miscreants dug through the temple walls and stole money, and on the night of 21 May 2024 the shrine was desecrated - the door broken, sacred garments and ritual items of Ibudhou and Ibendhou burnt, and two sacred boulders dented - an incident condemned by titular king Leishemba Sanajaoba and the Federation of Indigenous People's Democratic Movement. name: Pakhangba Temple, Thoubal
town: Uyal (Thoubal district; CSV town 'Thoubal' is the district headquarters)
town_description: Uyal is a village in Thoubal district of Manipur, set in the Imphal valley at the foot of the Uyal Cheirao Ching hill, which lies inside the Gwarok Reserved Forest. The surrounding villages - Wangbal, Kairembikhok, Wangjing, Salungpham, Heirok - are agrarian Meitei settlements whose residents climb the hill to the Pakhangba shrine. The nearest town is Thoubal, the district headquarters, and Imphal is about 22 km to the northwest.
